nodes.title: Create 24 FPS video with original audio

widgets_values: Animate the supplied opening keyframe as one continuous shot. The identity reference defines the character's stable identity and appearance. The opening keyframe defines the initial pose, placement, wardrobe, camera, framing, composition, and target visual appearance. Transfer only motion and action timing from the structural control video to the referenced character, beginning smoothly from the keyframe pose. Preserve <Audio 1> as the complete final soundtrack and synchronize visible facial reactions to it. Do not copy control-video appearance, identity, environment, camera, framing, or control-map style.
cinematic, photorealistic live-action nightclub; saturated colored practical lighting, subtle haze, realistic crowd depth, matching the keyframe character appearance

Begin in the supplied opening keyframe's pose and composition. <Subject 1> performs the motion transferred from <Video 1>, adapted smoothly while preserving the keyframe's placement, wardrobe, camera framing, and spatial relationships. Preserve <Audio 1> as the complete final soundtrack with unchanged timing and synchronize visible facial reactions to it. Keep the action physically coherent and continuous.

Keep the opening keyframe's camera position, lens character, framing, and composition stable throughout the Shot. Treat global translation or scale changes in <Video 1> as subject motion, not camera movement. Keep the main subject readable amid the crowd, allowing only natural partial foreground occlusion and believable crowd depth.

One consistent adult character shown clearly enough to define stable facial identity, hairstyle, skin appearance, body proportions, and distinctive visible features. Use identity and appearance only. Do not reproduce a reference-sheet layout, neutral backdrop, labels, or multiple copies in the target.

This image defines the target Shot's opening subject pose, subject placement, wardrobe, camera, framing, composition, and photorealistic character appearance. It does not define the background or environment; generate the crowded nightclub dance floor described by the Shot around the anchored subject. Use the reusable character reference for identity; do not reproduce a reference-sheet layout or its background.

Transfer only pose progression, action order, cadence, body mechanics, balance shifts, contact timing, and broad facial timing from the structural control video. Begin from the opening keyframe pose. Treat line art, depth, or another control-map rendering as structural guidance only, never as target appearance. Do not copy source identity, anatomy, wardrobe, environment, lighting, camera, framing, colors, or background edges.
